name: University of California, Santa Barbara
header:
University of California, Santa Barbara
United States · Mathematics PhD or PhD/MA
Rank verified separately
Eligibility and preparation · Deadlines by stage · English and GRE · Academic records · Recommendation letters · Written
materials · Funding and fees · Conflicts and remaining checks · Faculty · Sources
Pay attention to
• Math GRE required; General GRE submissions prohibited.
• Deadline conflict is material: directory December 16 versus department December 15.
• Minimum 250 words for Personal History Statement; required advanced-course descriptions and textbooks.
• IDRF resolves later international NRST under conditions but does not cover first year.
• Representation-theory research pages include emeriti; current personnel roster takes precedence.
• Faculty shortlist covers direct algebra/arithmetic/complex and quantum-category fits; broader differential
geometry/analysis faculty are not fully enumerated.

sections.title: Eligibility and preparation
sections.text:
Eligibility for your route [Standing rule]
Eligible in principle with a mathematics/related bachelor's completed before enrollment and undergraduate
GPA at least 3.0. International status is allowed. For applicants without a master's, central instructions
recommend selecting the combined PhD/MA where available; this differs from the UCSB-undergraduate-only
five-year combined program. [s3] [s4] [s5]
Before submission [Standing rule]
Choose Mathematics PhD/MA or confirm the appropriate objective with math-gradinfo@math.ucsb.edu. Prepare
the required Math GRE, three referees, two statements, CV and course descriptions/textbooks. Only one UCSB
application per year is allowed. No prior supervisor agreement is listed. [s1] [s2] [s3] [s5]
Adviser contact [Standing rule]
No advance adviser agreement stated. Direct requirements/deadline questions to
math-gradinfo@math.ucsb.edu. Contact research faculty to ask about 2027 capacity; current affiliation does
not establish openings. Zhao's official advice expects prospective students in his area to learn
schemes/sheaves/cohomology by the end of their second PhD year. [s1] [s39]
Portal workflow [Standing rule]
Slate application and Applicant Portal are linked by Graduate Division. Final submission is irreversible; content
cannot generally be changed afterward, although checklist items/references have their own controls. Upload
only required supporting documents. Use the live Requirements & Deadlines screen to resolve older
page/interface language. [s4] [s6]
Cycle verification [Conflict]
Explicit Fall 2027 program-directory records and 2027 university admissions manual available; department
deadline/cycle wording lags them. October 2027 TA salary rates are contractual, but the actual Math funding
package remains individual. [s1] [s2] [s3] [s11] [s17]

sections.title: Deadlines by stage
sections.text:
Academic application [Conflict]
Fall 2027 live directory: Wednesday, December 16, 2026. The department instead publishes December 15,
2026 while incorrectly calling the coming quarter Fall 2026. The new university standardized schedule supports
December 16, but the discrepancy requires confirmation. Math-specific hour/timezone not published in
checked sources. Practical safeguard: complete everything by December 15. [s1] [s2] [s3] [s40]
Funding consideration [Conflict]
The Fall 2027 directory has no separate priority financial deadline; departmental instructions require all items
and fee by December 15 for every form of support. Confirm whether the new December 16 deadline also
governs funding. University nominations occur in January; that internal schedule is not an extension for
applicants. [s1] [s3] [s8] [s11]
Reference receipt [Conflict]
Three letters must accompany the complete application by the department deadline. No guaranteed separate
letter grace period found; December 15 versus December 16 conflict applies. Contact the program before
relying on any late submission. [s3] [s5] [s6]
Test-score receipt [Conflict]
Official required Math GRE and any required language scores must be received by the application deadline;
allow three to four weeks for processing. ETS code 4835, department code unnecessary. GRE validity five
years; language scores two years at submission. Most recent complete score report is used, not superscoring.
No guaranteed late-score window. [s3] [s5] [s6]
Supporting documents [Conflict]
Application uploads/fee due with the complete file; December 15/16 conflict above. For admitted fall students,
the international-admit page gives September 1 for final official documents, whereas the application guide
says before instruction begins. Use the earlier September 1 planning date and verify the decision letter's 2027
requirement. [s3] [s4] [s12]
Accepting an offer [2027 confirmed]
The official 2027 staff guide sets April 15 for accepting financial support and submitting the online Statement
of Intent to Register (SIR). Final SIR deadline for all admitted applicants is June 15; later SIR needs an
exception. Emailing the department does not replace the online SIR. Exact cutoff hour not stated. [s11]

sections.title: English and GRE
sections.text:
English requirement [Standing rule]
TOEFL iBT: 4.0 for tests on/after January 21, 2026, or 80 on the older scale; IELTS 7; Duolingo 120. Home
Edition/approved academic online formats accepted; TOEFL Essentials/ITP Plus and IELTS One Skill Retake are
not. Teaching certification is separate. [s1] [s5]
UChicago English exemption [Standing rule]
A completed UChicago bachelor's qualifies under the accredited US English-only degree route. Public wording
says completed: if the degree remains in progress at application, ask whether an anticipatory exemption is
available. Completing the entire undergraduate degree in English also exempts Grad ELPE placement, after
verification. Non-native-English prospective TAs still require the TA language evaluation. [s4] [s12]
GRE General [Standing rule]
Not accepted: the department explicitly instructs applicants not to submit General GRE scores. [s3]
GRE Mathematics [2027 confirmed]
Required for Fall 2027. Official ETS reporting is necessary; no minimum score published. [s1]

sections.title: Academic records
sections.text:
Transcripts and degree records [Standing rule]
Upload registrar-issued transcript PDFs for every postsecondary institution attended for one full
term/equivalent, including summer/community-college study, with grading key. Maximum 9 MB, printable on
US letter paper; degree audits are not acceptable. Do not mail originals initially. US degrees use final
institutional transcripts; foreign degrees require WES ICAP after admission. [s1] [s4] [s12]
Mathematics-course list [2027 confirmed]
Required: mathematics beyond elementary calculus, differential equations and linear algebra, including
courses planned before enrollment. [s1]
Course descriptions [Standing rule]
The required math-course document includes course descriptions and references to textbooks used. No
separate syllabus requirement or page limit published. [s3]

sections.title: Recommendation letters
sections.text:
Number and type [Standing rule]
Three required; academic references preferred. Portal accepts up to four electronic letters. [s1] [s5]
Scholarship references [Standing rule]
Entry central fellowships use the admission record and departmental nomination. No additional external
reference is specified publicly; annual detailed nomination procedures are internal on GradPoint. Later
dissertation awards require a faculty-mentor letter and are not entry applications. [s13] [s14] [s16]
What sends the invitation [Standing rule]
Invitation is sent when the recommender is added using Send to Recommender; review details first. It does not
wait for final application submission. [s4] [s5]
Before versus after submission [Standing rule]
No: requests can be sent before final application submission. Adding a referee is an email-triggering action. [s4]
[s5]
Receipt confirmation [Standing rule]
Applicant checklist shows received/awaiting status, green check/red X and receipt date. Send Reminder is
available from the recommender record. [s5]
Updating and reusing letters [Unresolved]
Existing referee details cannot be edited; exclude and re-add/correct instead, and notify the excluded referee.
Letter services such as Interfolio are allowed, with both service and referee contact emails. Submitted-letter
replacement and automatic reuse in a new cycle are not established. [s4] [s5]

sections.title: Written materials
sections.text:
Academic CV / resume [Standing rule]
Required upload. Prompt paraphrase: employment, volunteering and community service since high school,
with dates, duties and weekly hours. No public length/typography limit. Omit General GRE information because
Math does not accept that exam. [s1] [s3]
Statement of purpose [Standing rule]
Required narrative upload. Prompt paraphrase: graduate-study motivation, intended specialization, previous
academic preparation and career plans, plus evidence of aptitude for UCSB. Avoid repeating the Personal
History Statement. No hard public maximum; FAQ suggests approximately two pages or more. Font/spacing
limits not established. [s1] [s5]

Personal / background statement [Standing rule]
Required essay upload, minimum 250 words, no maximum; commonly one to two pages. Prompt paraphrase:
relevant background, achievements, economic obstacles and varied experiences or service that contribute to
the graduate community. Do not duplicate the SOP. No font/spacing rule found. [s2]
Research-interest statement [Standing rule]
Included in the SOP and program-interest selections; no separate research-interest document listed. The
application also permits brief research/teaching experience entries that complement the SOP; exact character
caps not public. [s3] [s4]
Research proposal [Standing rule]
Not requested as a separate requirement. The directory lists no other required submission; central instructions
prohibit unsolicited supplemental documents. No proposal upload/link should be assumed permitted. [s1] [s4]
Writing sample / thesis / research summary [2027 confirmed]
Explicitly not required in the Fall 2027 directory; do not upload unsolicited thesis/papers as additional
documents. [s1] [s4]
Publications list [Standing rule]
No separate publications-list requirement or permission to upload/link full papers found. Relevant academic
work can be described in the CV/SOP; extra documents are prohibited unless required. [s1] [s4]
Course-list document [Conflict]
Required course document: completed/planned advanced mathematics with descriptions and textbooks.
Department says upload under other document type in supplemental documents; current directory labels it
Department Form. Confirm the live slot/template, which takes precedence over older interface names.
Length/typography not published. [s1] [s3]
Scholarship essays [Standing rule]
No separate entry scholarship essay listed. Nomination guidance uses SOP/personal statement to explain merit
and, where relevant, economic/educational obstacles or service to disadvantaged communities (paraphrase).
Department supplies nomination; award-specific extra questions are in its annual internal memo and must be
checked if nominated. [s14] [s16]
Other short answers / materials [Standing rule]
Optional application research-program/professional-experience entries; public guide suggests a few sentences
for research/teaching experience. If outside funding already awarded, report agency, amount/duration and
upload award letter; the uploaded letter cannot be deleted. No further Math requirement listed. [s2] [s4]

sections.title: Funding and fees
sections.text:
Amount and coverage [2027 confirmed]
No fixed Mathematics offer amount is published. Binding UC scale effective October 1, 2027: Group 1 TA at
50% appointment, entry salary point, USD 4,278/month; nine paid months would equal USD 38,502 gross by
arithmetic, not a guaranteed year-round offer. Current October 2026 rate is USD 4,100/month (USD 36,900 for
nine months). Summer, appointment percentage and first September timing require the individual offer.
Qualifying appointments remit tuition, specified fees and health premiums. [s8] [s17] [s18] [s19] [s41]
Years of support [Standing rule]
Good-progress PhD students can normally expect five years, but the department describes annual competitive
allocation rather than an unconditional five-year guarantee. Campus fellowship packages may span one to five
years. Multi-year commitments must be written in the offer with each year's support defined. [s8] [s16]
International eligibility [Standing rule]
International doctoral students are eligible for assistantships and automatic IDRF. IDRF covers nonresident
supplemental tuition from the fourth quarter until candidacy, conditional on timely progress/good standing; it

does not cover year one. After candidacy, nonresident tuition is waived for up to nine registered quarters.
Verify year-one NRST funding in the offer. Federal need-based loans/work-study listed by Math are restricted to
US citizens/permanent residents. [s8] [s9] [s10]
Conditions and duties [Standing rule]
Typical TA work is 16-20 hours/week, with first-fall training and spoken-English certification. At least 25%
qualifying employment yields tuition/student-services/campus-fee remission and full student health premium
remission under the contract; NRST has separate rules. Central fellows need full-time eight-unit enrollment,
GPA/progress standards and continuous registration. Summer eligibility is conditional and not a summer award
guarantee. [s8] [s15] [s18] [s19]
Extra funding application [Standing rule]
Indicate funding interests and outside awards in the application; that section is not a standalone fellowship
application. Entry central awards are department-nominated using the admission file. IDRF is automatic for
qualifying incoming international PhD students. No distinct Math assistantship essay or application is
published. [s4] [s10] [s13] [s16]
Other funding routes [Standing rule]
Campus/department fellowships, TAs, advanced-student teaching associateships, reader appointments and
adviser-funded GSRs are separate possibilities. Later opportunities include international-eligible
Broida-Hirschfelder (published USD 5,000-10,500 for a fall quarter; March 6, 2026 deadline is prior cycle) and
dissertation fellowships. Their continuation-stage conditions are not initial admission promises. [s8] [s13]
Application fee [Conflict]
USD 155 for an F-1 international applicant; USD 135 applies only to US citizens/permanent residents.
Nonrefundable; payment must be received by the deadline. The guide permits credit-card payment through
the portal after submission, whereas FAQ wording says at submission; plan to pay promptly within the
deadline. [s3] [s4] [s5]
Fee waiver [Standing rule]
Central fee waivers are unavailable to international applicants. Eligible domestic requests must be lodged at
least one week before the deadline through the application with supporting evidence; this is not an available
F-1 route. No public Math-funded international waiver found. [s7]

text:
University of California, Santa Barbara
United States · Mathematics PhD or PhD/MA
Rank verified separately
Eligibility and preparation · Deadlines by stage · English and GRE · Academic records · Recommendation letters · Written
materials · Funding and fees · Conflicts and remaining checks · Faculty · Sources
Pay attention to
• Math GRE required; General GRE submissions prohibited.
• Deadline conflict is material: directory December 16 versus department December 15.
• Minimum 250 words for Personal History Statement; required advanced-course descriptions and textbooks.
• IDRF resolves later international NRST under conditions but does not cover first year.
• Representation-theory research pages include emeriti; current personnel roster takes precedence.
• Faculty shortlist covers direct algebra/arithmetic/complex and quantum-category fits; broader differential
geometry/analysis faculty are not fully enumerated.
Eligibility and preparation
Eligibility for your route [Standing rule]
Eligible in principle with a mathematics/related bachelor's completed before enrollment and undergraduate
GPA at least 3.0. International status is allowed. For applicants without a master's, central instructions
recommend selecting the combined PhD/MA where available; this differs from the UCSB-undergraduate-only
five-year combined program. [s3] [s4] [s5]
Before submission [Standing rule]
Choose Mathematics PhD/MA or confirm the appropriate objective with math-gradinfo@math.ucsb.edu. Prepare
the required Math GRE, three referees, two statements, CV and course descriptions/textbooks. Only one UCSB
application per year is allowed. No prior supervisor agreement is listed. [s1] [s2] [s3] [s5]
Adviser contact [Standing rule]
No advance adviser agreement stated. Direct requirements/deadline questions to
math-gradinfo@math.ucsb.edu. Contact research faculty to ask about 2027 capacity; current affiliation does
not establish openings. Zhao's official advice expects prospective students in his area to learn
schemes/sheaves/cohomology by the end of their second PhD year. [s1] [s39]
Portal workflow [Standing rule]
Slate application and Applicant Portal are linked by Graduate Division. Final submission is irreversible; content
cannot generally be changed afterward, although checklist items/references have their own controls. Upload
only required supporting documents. Use the live Requirements & Deadlines screen to resolve older
page/interface language. [s4] [s6]
Cycle verification [Conflict]
Explicit Fall 2027 program-directory records and 2027 university admissions manual available; department
deadline/cycle wording lags them. October 2027 TA salary rates are contractual, but the actual Math funding
package remains individual. [s1] [s2] [s3] [s11] [s17]

Deadlines by stage
Academic application [Conflict]
Fall 2027 live directory: Wednesday, December 16, 2026. The department instead publishes December 15,
2026 while incorrectly calling the coming quarter Fall 2026. The new university standardized schedule supports
December 16, but the discrepancy requires confirmation. Math-specific hour/timezone not published in
checked sources. Practical safeguard: complete everything by December 15. [s1] [s2] [s3] [s40]
Funding consideration [Conflict]
The Fall 2027 directory has no separate priority financial deadline; departmental instructions require all items
and fee by December 15 for every form of support. Confirm whether the new December 16 deadline also
governs funding. University nominations occur in January; that internal schedule is not an extension for
applicants. [s1] [s3] [s8] [s11]
Reference receipt [Conflict]
Three letters must accompany the complete application by the department deadline. No guaranteed separate
letter grace period found; December 15 versus December 16 conflict applies. Contact the program before
relying on any late submission. [s3] [s5] [s6]
Test-score receipt [Conflict]
Official required Math GRE and any required language scores must be received by the application deadline;
allow three to four weeks for processing. ETS code 4835, department code unnecessary. GRE validity five
years; language scores two years at submission. Most recent complete score report is used, not superscoring.
No guaranteed late-score window. [s3] [s5] [s6]
Supporting documents [Conflict]
Application uploads/fee due with the complete file; December 15/16 conflict above. For admitted fall students,
the international-admit page gives September 1 for final official documents, whereas the application guide
says before instruction begins. Use the earlier September 1 planning date and verify the decision letter's 2027
requirement. [s3] [s4] [s12]
Accepting an offer [2027 confirmed]
The official 2027 staff guide sets April 15 for accepting financial support and submitting the online Statement
of Intent to Register (SIR). Final SIR deadline for all admitted applicants is June 15; later SIR needs an
exception. Emailing the department does not replace the online SIR. Exact cutoff hour not stated. [s11]
English and GRE
English requirement [Standing rule]
TOEFL iBT: 4.0 for tests on/after January 21, 2026, or 80 on the older scale; IELTS 7; Duolingo 120. Home
Edition/approved academic online formats accepted; TOEFL Essentials/ITP Plus and IELTS One Skill Retake are
not. Teaching certification is separate. [s1] [s5]
UChicago English exemption [Standing rule]
A completed UChicago bachelor's qualifies under the accredited US English-only degree route. Public wording
says completed: if the degree remains in progress at application, ask whether an anticipatory exemption is
available. Completing the entire undergraduate degree in English also exempts Grad ELPE placement, after
verification. Non-native-English prospective TAs still require the TA language evaluation. [s4] [s12]
GRE General [Standing rule]
Not accepted: the department explicitly instructs applicants not to submit General GRE scores. [s3]
GRE Mathematics [2027 confirmed]
Required for Fall 2027. Official ETS reporting is necessary; no minimum score published. [s1]

Academic records
Transcripts and degree records [Standing rule]
Upload registrar-issued transcript PDFs for every postsecondary institution attended for one full
term/equivalent, including summer/community-college study, with grading key. Maximum 9 MB, printable on
US letter paper; degree audits are not acceptable. Do not mail originals initially. US degrees use final
institutional transcripts; foreign degrees require WES ICAP after admission. [s1] [s4] [s12]
Mathematics-course list [2027 confirmed]
Required: mathematics beyond elementary calculus, differential equations and linear algebra, including
courses planned before enrollment. [s1]
Course descriptions [Standing rule]
The required math-course document includes course descriptions and references to textbooks used. No
separate syllabus requirement or page limit published. [s3]
Recommendation letters
Number and type [Standing rule]
Three required; academic references preferred. Portal accepts up to four electronic letters. [s1] [s5]
Scholarship references [Standing rule]
Entry central fellowships use the admission record and departmental nomination. No additional external
reference is specified publicly; annual detailed nomination procedures are internal on GradPoint. Later
dissertation awards require a faculty-mentor letter and are not entry applications. [s13] [s14] [s16]
What sends the invitation [Standing rule]
Invitation is sent when the recommender is added using Send to Recommender; review details first. It does not
wait for final application submission. [s4] [s5]
Before versus after submission [Standing rule]
No: requests can be sent before final application submission. Adding a referee is an email-triggering action. [s4]
[s5]
Receipt confirmation [Standing rule]
Applicant checklist shows received/awaiting status, green check/red X and receipt date. Send Reminder is
available from the recommender record. [s5]
Updating and reusing letters [Unresolved]
Existing referee details cannot be edited; exclude and re-add/correct instead, and notify the excluded referee.
Letter services such as Interfolio are allowed, with both service and referee contact emails. Submitted-letter
replacement and automatic reuse in a new cycle are not established. [s4] [s5]
Written materials
Academic CV / resume [Standing rule]
Required upload. Prompt paraphrase: employment, volunteering and community service since high school,
with dates, duties and weekly hours. No public length/typography limit. Omit General GRE information because
Math does not accept that exam. [s1] [s3]
Statement of purpose [Standing rule]
Required narrative upload. Prompt paraphrase: graduate-study motivation, intended specialization, previous
academic preparation and career plans, plus evidence of aptitude for UCSB. Avoid repeating the Personal
History Statement. No hard public maximum; FAQ suggests approximately two pages or more. Font/spacing
limits not established. [s1] [s5]

Personal / background statement [Standing rule]
Required essay upload, minimum 250 words, no maximum; commonly one to two pages. Prompt paraphrase:
relevant background, achievements, economic obstacles and varied experiences or service that contribute to
the graduate community. Do not duplicate the SOP. No font/spacing rule found. [s2]
Research-interest statement [Standing rule]
Included in the SOP and program-interest selections; no separate research-interest document listed. The
application also permits brief research/teaching experience entries that complement the SOP; exact character
caps not public. [s3] [s4]
Research proposal [Standing rule]
Not requested as a separate requirement. The directory lists no other required submission; central instructions
prohibit unsolicited supplemental documents. No proposal upload/link should be assumed permitted. [s1] [s4]
Writing sample / thesis / research summary [2027 confirmed]
Explicitly not required in the Fall 2027 directory; do not upload unsolicited thesis/papers as additional
documents. [s1] [s4]
Publications list [Standing rule]
No separate publications-list requirement or permission to upload/link full papers found. Relevant academic
work can be described in the CV/SOP; extra documents are prohibited unless required. [s1] [s4]
Course-list document [Conflict]
Required course document: completed/planned advanced mathematics with descriptions and textbooks.
Department says upload under other document type in supplemental documents; current directory labels it
Department Form. Confirm the live slot/template, which takes precedence over older interface names.
Length/typography not published. [s1] [s3]
Scholarship essays [Standing rule]
No separate entry scholarship essay listed. Nomination guidance uses SOP/personal statement to explain merit
and, where relevant, economic/educational obstacles or service to disadvantaged communities (paraphrase).
Department supplies nomination; award-specific extra questions are in its annual internal memo and must be
checked if nominated. [s14] [s16]
Other short answers / materials [Standing rule]
Optional application research-program/professional-experience entries; public guide suggests a few sentences
for research/teaching experience. If outside funding already awarded, report agency, amount/duration and
upload award letter; the uploaded letter cannot be deleted. No further Math requirement listed. [s2] [s4]
Funding and fees
Amount and coverage [2027 confirmed]
No fixed Mathematics offer amount is published. Binding UC scale effective October 1, 2027: Group 1 TA at
50% appointment, entry salary point, USD 4,278/month; nine paid months would equal USD 38,502 gross by
arithmetic, not a guaranteed year-round offer. Current October 2026 rate is USD 4,100/month (USD 36,900 for
nine months). Summer, appointment percentage and first September timing require the individual offer.
Qualifying appointments remit tuition, specified fees and health premiums. [s8] [s17] [s18] [s19] [s41]
Years of support [Standing rule]
Good-progress PhD students can normally expect five years, but the department describes annual competitive
allocation rather than an unconditional five-year guarantee. Campus fellowship packages may span one to five
years. Multi-year commitments must be written in the offer with each year's support defined. [s8] [s16]
International eligibility [Standing rule]
International doctoral students are eligible for assistantships and automatic IDRF. IDRF covers nonresident
supplemental tuition from the fourth quarter until candidacy, conditional on timely progress/good standing; it

does not cover year one. After candidacy, nonresident tuition is waived for up to nine registered quarters.
Verify year-one NRST funding in the offer. Federal need-based loans/work-study listed by Math are restricted to
US citizens/permanent residents. [s8] [s9] [s10]
Conditions and duties [Standing rule]
Typical TA work is 16-20 hours/week, with first-fall training and spoken-English certification. At least 25%
qualifying employment yields tuition/student-services/campus-fee remission and full student health premium
remission under the contract; NRST has separate rules. Central fellows need full-time eight-unit enrollment,
GPA/progress standards and continuous registration. Summer eligibility is conditional and not a summer award
guarantee. [s8] [s15] [s18] [s19]
Extra funding application [Standing rule]
Indicate funding interests and outside awards in the application; that section is not a standalone fellowship
application. Entry central awards are department-nominated using the admission file. IDRF is automatic for
qualifying incoming international PhD students. No distinct Math assistantship essay or application is
published. [s4] [s10] [s13] [s16]
Other funding routes [Standing rule]
Campus/department fellowships, TAs, advanced-student teaching associateships, reader appointments and
adviser-funded GSRs are separate possibilities. Later opportunities include international-eligible
Broida-Hirschfelder (published USD 5,000-10,500 for a fall quarter; March 6, 2026 deadline is prior cycle) and
dissertation fellowships. Their continuation-stage conditions are not initial admission promises. [s8] [s13]
Application fee [Conflict]
USD 155 for an F-1 international applicant; USD 135 applies only to US citizens/permanent residents.
Nonrefundable; payment must be received by the deadline. The guide permits credit-card payment through
the portal after submission, whereas FAQ wording says at submission; plan to pay promptly within the
deadline. [s3] [s4] [s5]
Fee waiver [Standing rule]
Central fee waivers are unavailable to international applicants. Eligible domestic requests must be lodged at
least one week before the deadline through the application with supporting evidence; this is not an available
F-1 route. No public Math-funded international waiver found. [s7]
Conflicts and remaining checks
Conflicting sources [Conflict]
December 16, 2026 in current directory versus December 15 on Math pages; department's Fall 2026 label
conflicts with that date. Final official records: September 1 on admitted-international page versus first
instruction day in general guide. Department warning about later NRST omits central IDRF coverage. Current
roster marks Goodearl, Huisgen-Zimmermann, Stopple and Yitang Zhang emeriti despite research-group
listings. [s1] [s3] [s4] [s8] [s10] [s12] [s20] [s21] [s22]
Checks still needed [Unresolved]
Confirm December 15/16 and cutoff timezone for every item/funding; anticipatory English exemption if
UChicago degree unfinished; current course-list upload slot; SOP/CV formatting; submitted-letter replacement;
2027 Math monthly schedule, summer and year-one NRST coverage; fellowship nomination extras; and adviser
availability. [s1] [s3] [s4] [s5] [s8] [s16]
